sites.name: AgentReplay
sites.tagline: Record once. Replay bit-exact. Zero model calls.
sites.summary: Deterministic replay and counterfactual debugging for AI agents. Record a live run, then replay it exactly — without spending another token — and branch it to ask what-if. Born from a year of shipping agents in production.

features.title: Bit-exact replay
features.body: Every recorded run reproduces with 100% fidelity and zero model calls — the bug you saw is the bug you get back.

features.title: Counterfactual branching
features.body: Fork a recorded run, change one prompt or parameter, and observe exactly where the trajectories diverge.

features.title: Call-site canonicalization
features.body: Every external call is recorded against a stable identity, so replay survives refactors and retries.

features.title: Content-addressed blob store
features.body: Recorded runs deduplicate naturally — storage stays small even across thousands of traces.

features.title: SDK interceptors
features.body: OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs and LangGraph supported out of the box. No forking, no wrappers rewrites.

features.title: CI regression for agents
features.body: Replay saved runs on every commit and fail the build on behavioral drift — testing, finally, for nondeterministic software.

sites.name: Verxlite
sites.tagline: The AI workflow agent for teams with no ML team.
sites.summary: A universal AI workflow agent for sales and operations. Connect your Google and HubSpot accounts, compose workflows, and let the agent run — with every step traced and every credential encrypted.

features.title: Workflow engine on Celery
features.body: Long-running, retryable, observable pipelines — automation that survives Monday morning, not just the demo.

features.title: Native CRM integrations
features.body: Google and HubSpot OAuth out of the box; tokens stored with Fernet encryption, never in plaintext.

features.title: Langfuse tracing on every step
features.body: The full chain from trigger to outcome — not just the final answer. Debug what actually happened.

features.title: FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic
features.body: A grown-up backend: typed, migrated, and versioned from day one.

features.title: Next.js 14 front end
features.body: Compose, monitor and iterate workflows from a single dashboard.

sites.name: Fraud Detection System
sites.tagline: Regulated-grade fraud scoring in Go, in real time.
sites.summary: An enterprise-grade real-time fraud scoring engine: seven independent detectors fused into one calibrated score, wrapped in the full production surface — case management, RBAC, observability and Kubernetes manifests.

features.title: 7 independent detectors
features.body: Each detector is explainable on its own — velocity, anomaly, graph and behavioral signals composed, not black-boxed.

features.title: Weighted ensemble + logistic calibration
features.body: Detector outputs fuse into one calibrated probability that risk teams can actually threshold.

features.title: Rules engine
features.body: Hard business constraints that must never wait on a model — sanctions, limits, geography — evaluated first.

features.title: Case management
features.body: Full investigation workflow with immutable event history: every score, override and outcome is auditable.

features.title: RBAC + JWT
features.body: Role-based access control with token auth across every surface.

features.title: Observability & deployment
features.body: Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry tracing, Slack alerting, and Kubernetes manifests — deployable, not just runnable.

sites.name: KilimoPRO
sites.tagline: Agritech that works on a $50 Android phone, offline.
sites.summary: Offline-first agricultural intelligence for 8 IGAD countries: on-device crop-disease detection, a five-persona AI council for complex decisions, 22 verified data sources, and SMS delivery for farmers without smartphones.

features.title: On-device disease detection
features.body: MobileNetV3 trained on PlantVillage, quantized to int8, running offline on low-end Android — no connectivity required.

features.title: Multi-LLM Council
features.body: Five expert personas — agronomist, economist, climate scientist, extension officer, risk manager — deliberate complex farming decisions.

features.title: 22 verified data sources
features.body: KilimoSTAT, FAOSTAT, KALRO, Google Earth Engine, Sentinel-2, CHIRPS, ICPAC and more — every source operational, not aspirational.

features.title: Quant finance for commodity prices
features.body: EWMA volatility, GARCH(1,1), Value at Risk and RSI applied to agricultural markets — forecasting with real statistics.

features.title: SMS delivery
features.body: Advice reaches farmers with feature phones, not just smartphones.

sites.name: IntelliFlow
sites.summary: A research platform for self-improving agent architectures: 33 agents that evolve their own prompts, orchestrated on a Turborepo + Next.js 15 backbone — built to test how far agents can go when they own their improvement loop.

features.title: 33-agent architecture
features.body: Specialized agents with distinct roles, sharing one orchestration backbone.

features.title: Self-evolving prompts
features.body: Agents propose and test improvements to their own instructions — evolution with evaluation gates.

features.title: Turborepo monorepo
features.body: Typed, cached and composed across packages; TypeScript throughout.

features.title: Next.js 15 surface
features.body: Observe the swarm, inspect evolutions, replay decisions.

sites.name: Financial Forecasting Suite
sites.summary: A time-series forecasting toolkit: Holt-Winters, ARIMA and ensemble methods with real validation — the statistical engines behind Busara AI's forecasts, packaged to be reused wherever forecasts drive decisions.

features.title: Holt-Winters
features.body: Triple exponential smoothing for seasonality and trend — implemented, tested, owned.

features.title: ARIMA
features.body: Classical autoregressive integrated moving-average models with proper order selection.

features.title: Ensemble combination
features.body: Methods combined with learned weights — better than any single model, honest about uncertainty.

features.title: Validation harness
features.body: Backtesting with walk-forward splits; the numbers that survive stakeholders.

sites.name: Customer Segmentation Engine
sites.tagline: Transaction noise in, actionable cohorts out.
sites.summary: RFM analysis fused with K-Means and Gaussian Mixture Models: turns raw transaction histories into segments a growth team can act on — with the statistical honesty to say when a cluster is not a cluster.

features.title: RFM core
features.body: Recency, frequency and monetary scoring — the foundation that always earns its place.

features.title: K-Means with silhouette validation
features.body: Clusters validated, not assumed; the engine says when structure is absent.

features.title: Gaussian Mixture Models
features.body: Soft assignments and probabilistic membership for the customers who live between segments.

features.title: Actionable output
features.body: Segments exported with profiles a growth team can target on Monday morning.

sites.name: FirstLight
sites.tagline: Geo-AI decision layer for the first 72 hours after a flood.
sites.summary: Damage and flood detection from SAR imagery, H3 priority zoning with need scoring, routing with isochrones, and hash-verified situation reports — every data layer provenance-labeled so responders know exactly what they are looking at.

features.title: SAR damage & flood detection
features.body: Satellite-derived damage layers rendered on an interactive MapLibre GL map.

features.title: H3 priority zoning
features.body: Res-8 hexagonal zoning with per-cell need scoring — transparent prioritization, not a black box.

features.title: Dijkstra routing + isochrones
features.body: Reachability, not just distance — where can help actually get, and how fast.

features.title: Hash-verified sitreps
features.body: Situation reports sealed with FNV-1a hashes; tampering is detectable.

features.title: Provenance labeling
features.body: Simulated layers are labeled simulated — the demo never lies about its data.
